question: Why is consciousness said to be independent of the means involving the knowable?
premises: The fire aspect is named Citrabhanu by the great Lord.
This naming reflects its self-luminous conscious nature.
Consciousness does not require external means beginning with the knowable.
inference: Because its nature is self-luminous fire, consciousness stands independent of the aggregate of means based on the knowable.
uncertainties: The verse ends mid-thought and continues into verse 126.
plain_english: For this reason the great Lord called this fire Citrabhanu. The status of consciousness is entirely independent of the whole set of means that begin with the knowable.
